title: Value of refresh_token in an X OAuth 2.0 token exchange
summary: A synthetic value of the refresh_token form field in a refresh request, shown as a curl --data-urlencode argument and a raw HTTP form body behind a Basic header placeholder, and of the refresh_token member in a token response excerpt.
rationale: X documents the refresh request as a form-encoded POST to the OAuth 2.0 token endpoint carrying refresh_token, grant_type=refresh_token and the client id (or a Basic header for a confidential client), and its token exchange page shows refresh_token as a member of the token response. The pages state no prefix, alphabet or width and the sample values in the curl examples are not a format, so the value is flagged because of the field or member it sits in, not because of its shape. The extent is the value only. The lifetime sentence on the exchange page is about the refresh token that exchange returns and is not used here. The client id, the scope list and the expires_in number are not values of this credential, and the access token of the same response is a different credential that these fixtures leave out.

expectation.rationale: Project policy, maintainer-only (ADR 0020, credential-evidence#235). Finalized by the sole maintainer alone: not reviewed, not independent validation, queued for retro-review (#154). The question, options, strongest dissent and reversing evidence are in the review history. Flagged under project policy: the value of an exact refresh_token form field of a token request or member of a token response is treated as a credential whatever its shape and covered whole. X documents the refresh_token form field of the refresh request and the refresh_token member of a token response shown for the same endpoint (carrier existence only); the value admission, extent and generic attribution are the project's decisions. No prefix, width or alphabet is claimed.

sources.supports: A refresh token allows an application to obtain a new access token without prompting the user. ... In addition, you will also need to pass in your refresh_token, set your grant_type to be a refresh_token, and define your client_id.

Success response (HTTP 200): {"token_type": "bearer", "expires_in": 7200, "access_token": "...", "refresh_token": "...", "scope": "..."}. Store the refresh_token (and current access_token) against the user

notes: Project-authored by the Redact Secret project, which maintains this repository; not independent evidence. Draft; not yet reviewed.
